fix_tasks.title: Ring 'seam bars': make the TIR bar and end block soft, D-shaped and noisy, and fade them on detached hold pieces
fix_tasks.evidence_summary: Hold-sweep MAJOR (+0.5). Crisp, parallel-edged, uniform darker-blue bars cross a ring band perpendicular to its tangent. They appear in idle/intro (sw_intro_3 x872-881 y324-382, sw_tau_2.75 x812-824 just inside the end cap, sw_tau_1.25 x758-803 and x837-870), in the pop (sw_pop_B x926-946 y319-417, the p04 blocks) and in the hold (sw_hold_L x910-922, sw_hold_TR). zoom_glitch_hold_sweep/bars_4x.png shows a flat steel-blue strip with a lighter block beyond it, which breaks the client's 'seamless rings' rule. Ice MAJOR (part of +0.5): a ruler-straight uniform stripe sits at band A's right corner (q00 x871-882 y346-415, q02 x872-882) where F000 has an irregular D-shaped dark corner (x866-880 y360-415), and a straight transverse stripe crosses the q02 ring end (x790-830 y263-303). Ice minor (+0.2): edge-on ring ends are opaque white with no horizon through them (q02 x593-680 y410-497).
fix_tasks.root_cause: This is the IceMaterial ICE_FRAG 'TIR bar' block (~lines 439-502). tbB is the distance of the UNREFRACTED line of sight (vCamRing) from the ring axis, and tbX = tbB - (uSectionRadius - uSectionHalf.x). Contours of constant tbB are planes through the camera, so they project as straight screen lines across the band near its apparent ends. tirBar is a window tbX in [-0.13, -0.02] m with only fwidth AA (tbAA), mixed to vec3(0.14,0.27,0.68) at a constant 0.8: that gives a ruler-straight, uniform bar. tirZone (tbX > -0.02) is the end block. Since #63 it does mix(body, mix(luma,body,0.6)*1.45, 0.85*tirZone) plus scatterLight*0.3, which makes a flat milky block behind a hard straight edge; that block is the 'opaque white ends'. vCamRing = camObj + uNoiseOffset, so every detached A quarter and B half computes its own bar in the pop and hold, at arbitrary places on the arcs. The front material has no 'detached' state; uJoined exists only on the back-depth material.
fix_tasks.implementation_plan:
0) Before any tuning in this plan, re-baseline. Deploys #64-#69 shipped AFTER the round-10 captures (#63). Run shoot_qc, shoot_pointer and shoot_sweep on #69 and re-measure every target on #69.
1) Confirm the cause with a probe_icevar variant tirBar = tirZone = 0 at sw_intro_3, sw_tau_2.75, sw_pop_B and sw_hold_L. The bars must vanish.
2) Make the bar D-shaped and jagged. After tbZ add: zr = saturate(abs(tbZ)/uSectionHalf.y); jag = (nA-0.5)*0.05 + b2.x*0.012. Set lo = -0.13*mix(0.5,1.0,sqrt(1-zr*zr)) + jag and hi = -0.02 + 0.5*jag. Use edge width w = max(tbAA, 0.012) m in all four smoothsteps of tirBar and tirZone.
3) Bar strength: replace the constant 0.8 with mix(0.45,0.72,nA). Change the colour to vec3(0.12,0.25,0.60), slightly darker so the corner holds its value with less coverage. Keep F *= 1-0.6*tirBar.
4) End block, which also fixes the opaque white ends: body = mix(body, mix(trans*tint*1.15, mix(vec3(lb),body,0.75)*1.2, 0.5), 0.45*tirZone). Drop the scatter add from 0.3 to 0.15 and keep the Â±8 % frost-noise luma. The refracted horizon then stays visible through the ends.
5) Detached pieces: add a uDetached uniform (0..1) to createIceMaterial. In Rings.update, in the loop that sets back.uJoined, compute per piece k = smoothstep(0.01, 0.2, |pivot.position - rest| + 2*(1-|pivot.quaternion.w|)) and write it to materials[i]. Then apply tirBar *= 1-0.75k and tirZone *= 1-0.6k. The value is continuous, so there are no pops.
6) Hold q00: the right band end (x860-890 y340-420) should keep a darker curved corner of about 135,165,200 (today's bar matched F000's 135,164,200). The end-block mean should land at about L170-180 (F000 L177).

fix_tasks.title: Lake reflection tears near the right floes off-centre: fade out the re-aim near a projector and cross-fade the straight fallback
fix_tasks.evidence_summary: Hold-sweep MAJOR (+0.4): floe reflection columns are cut by a hard horizontal line and continue shifted sideways. Cases: sw_hold_BL x1273-1293 at y659 (5 px); sw_pop_B x1270-1320 at y623 (18 px); p04 x1274-1300 y618-690, plus a vertical texture boundary at x~1295; sw_rel_TR x1235-1263 at y547, with a detached white rectangle at x1248-1263 y548-562; also sw_rel_BL and sw_hold_L (stairstep_stack3x.png). Centred p06 and rest are clean, so the tear jumps as the cursor moves. Cursor-orbit minor: a wavy 1-2 px dark hairline doubles the snowy rock's right silhouette on the water (ptr_left x440-446 y673-702, top_left, bottom_left).
fix_tasks.root_cause: Water.ts has binary lookup switches. For the rest projector: if (behind > 0.0) { if (sBehind <= 0.0) { pw = vWorldPos; pclip = vPlateClip; vis0 = 1.0; } }. The lookup jumps from plateMirrorPoint (re-aimed) to the straight lookup on the row where the re-aimed mirror point goes behind a floe. The two lookups differ by the reflection's parallax, so the column steps sideways. Every extra projector does the same in GLSL_WATER_PROJECTOR_BLEND (the `straight` flag), and that re-aim is already active at awayK > 0.02 m. The hold-sweep cameras sit 0.22 m off the hold projector (hold_L x -0.08 vs the projector at 0.14). Secondary sources: the `raised` test smoothstep(0.05,0.12) and visK make projector hand-offs at floe edges near-binary (probably the vertical boundary in p04); mirrorL's 'nearest reflector' rule (mx > 1.25 mn) is a hard switch; and the quv guard near rocks is binary, which drew the rock hairline.
fix_tasks.implementation_plan:
1) Bisect with a probe_water / probe_glitch tint: R where the rest straight fallback was taken, G where any extra projector used `straight`, B where mirrorL took the min across an edge. Capture sw_hold_BL, sw_pop_B, p04, sw_rel_TR. The step rows should coincide with a tint boundary.
2) Fade out the re-aim near a projector: reaimK = smoothstep(0.3, 1.2, camAway) for the rest projector, with the same ramp on awayK for each extra one, then pw = mix(vWorldPos, mirrorPoint, reaimK). At hold_L/R/BL/TR (0.22 m) all lookups become straight. That costs about 4 px of reflection parallax, which is acceptable.
3) Replace the binary fallback with a cross-fade. Inside the band -0.5 < behind < 1.5 m, sample both lookups (branch, so the second fetch runs only there). Weight wS = smoothstep(-0.3,0.8,behind)*(1 - smoothstep(-0.2,0.6,sBehind)); colour = mix(reaimed, straight, wS); vis0 = mix(vis0, 1, wS). Do the same in GLSL_WATER_PROJECTOR_BLEND.
4) If the p04 vertical boundary is a projector hand-off, soften `raised` to smoothstep(0.04,0.3,...) and average visK over 3 taps (Â±1.5 depth texels).
5) Rock hairline: scale `offs` by 0.2 when any of 4 depth taps 2-3 texels around cuv is more than 15 % nearer (an occluder edge).
6) Optional: a soft-min in mirrorL (weights exp(-(L-mn)/(0.25mn))), but only if step 1 shows blue tints at the steps.
fix_tasks.risk: Medium. The straight fallback (deploy #25) fixed the striped floe-shaped bands at the pointer extremes, and the raised test fixed rock and floe copies on the water. A cross-fade can leave a faint double column inside the band. Extra lake fetches cost T0 frame time in the hold (about 26 fps at scale 0.6 on a hot GPU), so keep them branched.

fix_tasks.title: Orb seen through the ice: replace the Gaussian glow floor with an analytic refracted-ray orb hit, and tint the orb light mint
fix_tasks.evidence_summary: Ice MAJOR (+0.6): the orb is never refracted. At p06, band A over the orb (x630-830 y370-460) is a soft milky-white smear, where F420 shows sharp white-cyan streaks (x600-847 y417-437) under a dark band (y403-417). p05 reads as 'white wax'. At q03, ring A over the orb is nearly invisible, while F045 shows a defined band with dark edges and a crack. Composition minor (+0.2): orb glare washes out the q03 inner 'eye' ring and swallows the innermost p07 rings. Orb MAJOR (+0.5): no teal/cyan glow on nearby ice. The hold band peaks at 234,242,247 vs 254,255,255. At rest, ring A over the orb is 185,200,215 (B-R 30) vs 193,213,235 (42), and ring D around the cap is too light. Colour lens: the halo around the orb is lavender, not mint.
fix_tasks.root_cause: IceMaterial ICE_FRAG, block 'Orb light carried by the ice': a FLOOR glowC = vec3(0.82,1.0,0.97)*uOrbGlow*2.4*lanternG*carry. lanternG is a Gaussian (sigma 1.15 orb radii) of the UNREFRACTED camera ray's distance to the orb. The floor fills wherever the ice is darker than it, times mix(0.45,1.2,frost). Every ring in front of the orb therefore lifts to a smooth near-white disc that ignores the facets, erasing the band's dark body, its rims and the q03 inner ring. The refraction copy carries the orb knee-compressed (BLIT_FRAG m' = 0.8 sqrt(m/0.8), so a core of 16 becomes 3.6), and the copy is sampled at uLensDepth 6 m while the orb sits about 1-2.5 m behind the bands. The true refracted orb is therefore neither bright nor in the right place. The proximity glow (0.07*prox, colour 0.9,0.95,1.0) is neutral. The orb radius 0.8255 is hard-coded three times.
fix_tasks.implementation_plan:
1) Add a shared uOrbRadius uniform: declare it in uniforms.ts, set it from the orb's uRadius each frame (Orb.syncTransform / HeroEngine), and replace the three hard-coded 0.8255 values.
2) Analytic hit along rdG (the facet-bent ray already computed): b = dot(rdG, P-C); c = |P-C|^2 - R^2; h2 = c - b*b; hn = sqrt(max(h2,0))/R. hit = step(b,0)*(1 - smoothstep(0.94 - 0.2*frost, 1.0, hn)). Lo = uOrbGlow*mix(vec3(0.80,1.0,0.95), vec3(1.0,1.0,0.98), 1-hn*hn)*(1.6 + 1.4*(1-hn)^2)*tint*(1-F), where tint carries the absorption. Then col = mix(col, max(col, Lo), hit*mix(0.9,0.55,frost)). Facets bend rdG differently, so the orb breaks into a mosaic of streaks, and rays that miss keep the band's dark body.
3) Floor: lower the 2.4 to 0.9, applied only where hit < 0.5. This keeps a faint lantern for frosted or TIR ice and preserves round 8's 'no dark pearl' guard.
4) Mint in-scatter: change the prox glow colour to vec3(0.72,1.0,0.94) and 0.07 to 0.10, weight it by mix(0.6,1.2,thick) and cap it at +0.15 luma. Change the orb spec glint colour to vec3(2.4,3.0,2.9).
5) Leave the RenderPipeline knee alone; it is what removed the milky veil.
6) Rebalance the sculpture mean (q00 x530-910 y215-525) with col *= 1.035 â†’ up to 1.06. Targets: q00 band over the orb L ~222 with sd >= 15 (F000 222); q03 band (x625-810 y350-415) with dark edges; p06 band x640-840 y400-450 with brightest 10 % >= 250 over a darker internal band.

fix_tasks.title: Thick-ice optics: steel-blue core bands from an analytic section exit (TIR along the tube), plus an analytic slab path that also feeds T0
fix_tasks.evidence_summary: Ice CRITICAL (+1.0): grey-white, under-saturated ice that lacks the saturated steel-blue bands along each tube. At q03, box x822-857 y300-420 measures L164, p10 143, sat 18 vs F045's 148 / 110 / 27; box x585-610 has sat 11 vs 19. q00 band A (x590-640) is 163,182,202 vs 174,196,226. F000 shows a dark band along the lower inner ring (x620-820 y440-460). Color MAJOR (+0.35): hero chroma is 15-36 % low, with no deep blue arc above the orb (y300: 190,201,212 vs 108,141,181). Composition minor: q00 C/D read as thin washers, while F000 shows a deep tunnel with a navy inner wall (x640-800 y290-310). Note: #65 multiplied the final ice chroma by 1.35 after the captures (eye-pose ring side sat 0.169 â†’ 0.209, F045 0.31). Chroma alone does not create the bands.
fix_tasks.root_cause: In the reference the bands come from the slab section's optics: light enters a face and meets a side wall past the critical angle (~50 deg at n = 1.31). IceMaterial only approximates this with masks: `band` (inward normals, suppressed where the refracted content is bright via 1 - smoothstep(0.3,0.6,tl)), `tir` (grazing Nr) and pathK. The macro lens is deliberately removed (tilt -= tiltMacro*(1-macroW)), so the section never bends the view. Thickness t comes from a half-res back-depth pass on T1+ and is the constant uBaseThickness 0.38 on T0 (backDepthScale 0), so T0's absorption cannot vary at all.
fix_tasks.implementation_plan:
1) Section exit, in ring-frame mesh units (about metres). pR = vObjPos/uObjScale; s0 = (length(pR.xy) - uSectionRadius, pR.z). Move objRd = refract(-objV, objN, 1/uIor) above the body. ds = (dot(objRd.xy, normalize(pR.xy)), objRd.z). Per wall, tw = (sign(ds)*uSectionHalf - s0)/ds, and tExit = min(tw). The entry face is the larger of |vSec.x| and |vSec.y|. disagreements:
Context: deploys #64-#69 shipped after the round-10 captures were taken on #63. They changed the orb smoke field (#64), ice chroma x1.35 (#65), the crushed-black toe including the floe slit (#66), the shard facet tint (#67), ripple contrast (#68), and the hold massif and bank, far haze, low mist and ridge slate (#69). Several verdicts below are therefore partly addressed already; re-baseline on #69 before tuning.
1) Orb in the hold. The orb lens wants 1.6-2x emission and a bloom halo; the colour lens measures 3.3x too much clipped area and wants less visible disc. My call: no gain increase. Hide most of the disc behind B's lens (T12) and add internal contrast: small clipped lobes and darker smoke lanes, with a tight halo on the lobes only (T10).
2) Orb rim. The orb lens wants a violet dispersion rim. The colour lens says today's ~9 px fringe is lavender and should be mint, and earlier rounds removed lavender (see the RAMP_COL note). My call: a 2-3 px violet outermost line with mint (G >= B) inside it.
3) Bloom. Composition wants the orb bloom capped at 0.6x for q03 and p07; the orb and colour lenses want a halo in the hold. My call: no wide bloom; only a fine-mip halo on clipped lobes (orb band threshold 7 â†’ 5).
4) Shards. The colour lens says they are too dark and saturated (84,119,209 vs 134,159,226). The orb lens says they show white chips and are not dark enough (wants 41,88,173). Awwwards says the mean matches but facet contrast is too high. My call: compress the facet range toward a lighter periwinkle mean, keep #67's white cap, and keep only a thin dark spine.
5) Ice surface. The ice lens wants smooth clear faces, tangential streaks and MORE blur through thick ice; Awwwards wants high-frequency crinkle everywhere and SHARPER refraction. My call: tangential streak frost plus a fine sparkle normal for the speculars. Blur only the background through long paths; the analytic orb hit (T08) keeps the orb crisp.
6) Ripples. Environment and Awwwards want bolder, darker troughs. Round 7 rejected bold rings as painted stripes, and #68 already lifted sd to 17.0 vs F000's 15.5, at L180 vs 186. My call: no more contrast. Use a wider wavelength and less grain, show the bands through the hero's reflection, and restore the mean.
7) Ice end blocks. Round 9 rejected saturated cobalt caps (#63 lifted them); round 10 calls them opaque white. My call: keep them neutral but let the refracted horizon through (T01).
8) TIR bars. Rounds 6-7 asked for F000's dark steel bars at the band ends; round 10's glitch hunter calls them seams and the ice judge calls them a ruler-straight stripe. My call: keep a darker band-end feature, but make it D-shaped, soft and noisy, and fade it on detached hold pieces.
9) Ring B at F402. Older code comments read 'no band across the orb' (bPortalSplit); the current composition judge measures a diagonal slab over the orb's upper half. My call: check ref_F402 directly before changing it; follow the judge if it confirms (T15).
10) Global grade. The colour lens proposes a -3 deg hue/white-balance shift and an S-curve with a lower black point. Yet its own sky values match within Â±1, and Awwwards says not to touch the grade. Its bottom-centre rocks read too light, while #66's data shows the bottom-left rocks' p1 darker than F000. My call: no global white-balance or curve change; local fixes only (T20).
11) Hold size. Awwwards suggests a ~20 % closer dolly; composition suggests more radial spread or a ~5 % dolly. My call: radial placement only (T12). The camera must stay on the hold plate's pose, so no new parallax or doubled plates.
12) Far-left ridge. Environment wants a re-bake (streaks and a trimmed silhouette); the colour lens says darkening alone will not do; #69 already made it slate in the shader. My call: keep #69, and do the silhouette and streaks only in the batched v8 re-bake (T22).
13) Hold foreground swell. Environment wants it, but four attempts (watervar2-5) failed. My call: lower priority. Bisect the bottom-strip path first, then try a directional rather than concentric swell (T16).
14) Idle loop at F12-F25. The judge's alternative ('reduce the pitch') conflicts with the matching ellipse. The evidence points to a Necker near-rim flip. My call: try a loop tip first, then a full-loop mirror A/B; a partial mirror window cannot be made seamless (T11).
